
6p-Block Triple-Zeta Basis Set Archive
======================================


Date: 17 Mar 2006


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, Theor. Chem. Acc. (2002) 108:335; erratum Theor. Chem. Acc. (2003) 109:284;
revision Theor. Chem. Acc. (2006) 115:441. Basis sets available from the Dirac web site, 
http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF spinor or orbital coefficients, 
given with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the basis sets described in the above articles. The d and f sets were reoptimized 
as follows: the outermost d function in the SCF set was replaced by the two valence 
correlating d functions, and the remaining SCF d exponents were reoptimized.
The outermost two f functions in the SCF set were replaced by the two core correlating
f functions,  and the remaining SCF f exponents were reoptimized. In the final SCF
calculations, the valence correlating f function was added to the f set. 
In all the following descriptions, this is the set referred to as the SCF
exponent set.

The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of diffuse s, p, d and f functions.

4. Exponents of valence correlating functions.

5. Exponents of core correlating functions.



Basis set construction.
----------------------

Several different types of basis sets may be constructed by adding primitive 
functions. These basis sets are described below.

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 

1. Valence (equivalent to cc-pvtz): To the SCF set add the following:
   1st and 3rd s primitives from the SCF set 
   1st and 3rd p primitives from the SCF set 
   1st and 2nd d primitives from the SCF set (valence correlating 2d)
   1st f primitive from the SCF set (valence correlating 1f)

   (HF + 2s2p2d1f valence)

2. Core-valence: To basis set 1, add the following:
   4th and 6th s primitives from the SCF set
   4th and 6th p primitives from the SCF set
   3rd and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   2nd and 3rd f primitives from the SCF set (core correlating 2f)
   core correlating 1g functions.

   (HF + 2s2p2d1f valence + 2s2p2d2f1g core)

3. Diffuse basis: add the diffuse s, p, d and f functions to any of the above
   basis sets.





Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================
